attribution.note: Marcus states and endorses this qualified comparison in his own words.

semantics.note: The normalisation preserves the retrospective comparison, uncertainty about his reading, and condition that the measures match.

contract.note: The contract reasonably identifies November 2024 and requires compatible evaluations without converting the qualified ranking into an unconditional claim.

evidence.note: The November paper reports 61.9% for an ensemble on public validation tasks, supporting the approximate numerical recollection only.
The released-o3 evaluation uses semi-private tasks. This establishes a mismatch with the paper's public validation split, not a contradiction of the conditional ranking.

reviews.rationale: The numerical recollection has support, but the comparative judgment is explicitly hedged and depends on matching measures. The cited evaluations use different task splits, so that condition is unmet. The vague similarity judgment supplies no separate scoring threshold. Neither support nor contradiction of the overall ranking is warranted.
